text: The 'bilking argument' is the most influential objection to backward causation. What does it purport to show?
choices: That backward causation is incoherent by definition, since a cause must be temporally prior to its effect
That any time-symmetric treatment of radiation must invoke advanced waves that violate the conservation of energy
That backward causation would generate a grandfather-style logical contradiction and so is outright impossible

That if a later event E caused an earlier event C, an agent could observe whether C had occurred and then bring about E only on occasions when C had not — systematically decoupling E from C and severing the alleged causal link
explanation: The bilking argument turns on the agent's ability to check the earlier effect C and then choose E so as to break the correlation, suggesting backward causation cannot be a stable feature of the world. Option 0 asserts the very conceptual-necessity thesis that Hume and Dummett reject (Dummett holds backward causation is coherent); option 1 misdescribes the Wheeler-Feynman theory; and option 2 conflates bilking with the separate grandfather paradox of time travel.
